title: Entitlement Tagging and SIEM Mapping Playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:

This playbook documents a pragmatic, low-friction approach to tagging entitlements (permissions/attributes) across services and mapping those tags into SIEM-friendly audit events and evidence bundles. It is intended for the security, platform, and SRE teams that will own RBAC v2 rollout and SIEM ingestion.

Goals:
- Ensure every permission decision in RBAC v2 is traceable to a stable entitlement tag and evidence artifact.
- Define a compact SIEM mapping that supports high-fidelity alerting and forensic queries without blowing up ingestion costs.
- Provide an automation path that generates evidence bundles and orchestrates evidence exports for compliance audits.
- Minimize developer friction: tagging conventions should be easy to apply and validate in CI.

Design principles:
1) Single-source tag identity: the canonical entitlement identifier is a short, dashed string (team:resource:action) registered in the Entitlement Registry. e.g. compute:inference-job:create
2) Attribute-forwarding in the stack: runtime systems (control plane, scheduler, agent) forward the entitlement tag with every request and include the tag in the audit envelope.
3) Compact SIEM events: SIEM payloads include a fixed set of fields (see Audit Schema) and embed the entitlement tag as both a primary field and a normalized tag array for lookups.
4) Evidence-as-code: evidence collection rules live next to policy definitions (YAML snippets) and are executed by the Evidence Agent to produce signed bundles.

Proposed entitlement tagging model:
- Namespace: <team>:<resource>:<action> (examples: platform:model:promote, product:console:impersonate)
- Level: read | write | admin | attestation (attached as metadata)
- Purpose: an optional free-text short ID to indicate why the permission exists (e.g. "billing-export")
- Version: semantic integer appended only when the entitlement semantics change in breaking ways (avoid churn)

Entitlement registry workflow:
- Registration: engineers open an entry in the Entitlement Registry (Confluence-backed form). A short review by security (48h SLA) verifies naming and purpose.
- Approval: approved entitlements receive a stable ID and are emitted to the central registry service.
- Deprecation: deprecated entitlements remain discoverable but marked with a deprecation timestamp and recommended replacement.

Audit log schema (compact SIEM-friendly):
Required top-level fields (string values unless noted):
- event_id: UUID
- timestamp: ISO8601
- principal_id: user/service id (prefer OIDC sub format)
- principal_type: user | service | unknown
- entitlement_id: canonical entitlement id (namespace:resource:action)
- resource_id: canonical resource identifier
- outcome: allow | deny | fail | fallback
- reason_code: short token for why outcome occurred (e.g. policy-mismatch, expired-token, emergency-bypass)
- request_context: short string (route or API name)
- service: service name producing audit (e.g. "control-plane")
Optional fields (included when available):
- client_ip
- region
- session_id
- request_payload_hash (sha256)
- evidence_bundle_id (reference to stored signed evidence)

SIEM mapping recommendations:
- Index entitlement_id and outcome as primary searchable fields. Create a composite index entitlement_id + outcome for quick "deny spikes" detection.
- Normalize tags: split entitlement_id into components (team, resource, action) in SIEM for flexible aggregation.
- Sample rate: high-volume internal health checks or automated agents should be sampled to 1% by default; any event with outcome != allow must be 100% forwarded.
- Alerting primitives: failed-or-deny-for-critical-resources, suspicious-privilege-escalation, cross-service-imposter-detection (based on unexpected principal_type).

Evidence automation design:
- Evidence Agent: a lightweight service that subscribes to audit events, captures additional context (stack traces, policy snapshots, policy-evaluator source commit), and produces a signed bundle.
- Bundle contents: event_id, entitlement_snapshot (policy version), policy-evaluator binary/commit, sanitized request/response payloads, TTL, signature, and provenance metadata.
- Storage: bundles stored in an immutable object store (WORM) with retention metadata. Evidence IDs are included in the audit log evidence_bundle_id field.
- Trigger rules: evidence bundles are produced for any of: outcome != allow, event touching "sensitive" resources (billing, keys, customer-data), or manually by investigator request.
- Automation pipeline: Evidence Agent -> signer -> WORM storage -> SIEM reference link generation -> export script for auditors.

SIEM export considerations and cost control:
- Do not export full payloads to SIEM. Store payloads in WORM and send only references and metadata to SIEM.
- Use a tiered export: critical events (deny/fail) export immediately; informational events can be batched hourly.
- Apply compression and field drop rules in the forwarder to reduce ingestion.

Rollout plan (phased):
Phase 0 - Sandbox (2 weeks):
- Implement registry prototype, entitlement tagging linter, minimal audit envelope in a single non-prod service.
- Validate downstream SIEM parsers with sample events.

Phase 1 - Pilot (6 weeks):
- Onboard 3 teams (control-plane, console, billing) to tag entitlements and emit the compact audit schema.
- Run Evidence Agent in passive mode (collect only, do not sign/store) to gauge bundle sizes and metadata needs.
- Iterate on sampling rules and SIEM indexing.

Phase 2 - Scoped rollout (8–12 weeks):
- Enforce entitlement linter in CI for selected repos; require entitlement_id on policy changes.
- Enable Evidence Agent signing and WORM storage for production-labeled events.
- Create dashboards and baseline alert rules in SIEM.

Phase 3 - Org-wide (quarterly milestone):
- Expand lint enforcement across org; deprecate legacy free-text permission logs.
- Complete automated export and auditor playbooks.
- Run tabletop exercise with legal/compliance using real evidence bundles.

Migration and backward compatibility:
- Bridge layer: introduce a translation component in the audit pipeline that maps legacy permission strings to entitlement_ids using a best-effort lookup table.
- Dual-write: for 3 months, produce both legacy log field and new audit schema to allow dashboards and alerts to be migrated gradually.

Testing and validation:
- CI linter: ensures every policy/PR that touches permission surfaces includes an entitlement_id tag and a matching registry entry.
- Synthetic replay: generate replayed traffic to validate SIEM parsing and alerting thresholds before enabling in prod.
- Evidence integrity checks: periodic verification that signed evidence bundles are verifiable against the signing key material.

Operational runbook (short):
- "Missing entitlement" in audit: create registry ticket and apply temporary mapping; follow up with code owner to add tag.
- Evidence retrieval for audit: use evidence_bundle_id from SIEM event to fetch from WORM storage; verify signature and package contents before export.
- SIEM cost spike: enable emergency sampling throttle and raise on-call paging for security to triage.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Registry governance model: centralized gatekeeping reduces noise but risks blocking dev velocity. Consider a hybrid: auto-approve low-risk namespaces.
- Evidence retention: legal may request multi-year retention for certain customer events; estimate cost impact before finalizing.
- Sampling policy: 1% default for agents is a starting point — we need observed ingestion numbers to tune.

Appendix A: example audit event (compact JSON)
{
  "event_id": "b5e4a2f0-9acd-4c2d-9a0e-123456789abc",
  "timestamp": "2026-01-19T22:14:55Z",
  "principal_id": "oidc|users|U-4321",
  "principal_type": "user",
  "entitlement_id": "platform:model:promote",
  "resource_id": "models/runs/2026-01-19-57",
  "outcome": "deny",
  "reason_code": "policy-mismatch",
  "request_context": "control-plane.promoteModel",
  "service": "control-plane",
  "evidence_bundle_id": "evid-bundle-00001234"
}

Appendix B: quick CI linter rule (pseudo-YAML)
- file_match: "**/policies/*.yaml"
- require_field: entitlement_id
- registry_lookup: true
- severity: error

Next steps:
- Review: security and three pilot teams to review within 1 week.
- Prototype: engineering infra to stand up registry and passive Evidence Agent in next sprint.
- Owner: Asha Patel (security) for project coordination; Marcus Li (platform) for registry implementation.

Notes to reviewers: this playbook favors evidence integrity and SIEM cost control over maximal verbosity in SIEM. If your team has a high-risk product surface (keys, customer PII, billing) call that out in review and we will mark entitlement tags as "sensitive" and force full bundle capture by policy.
